newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch PTT plans 1,100 job cuts.
newsitem.headline: Dutch PTT plans 1,100 job cuts.

text.p: Dutch post and telecoms group PTT Nederland NV said on Wednesday it planned to cut around 1,100 jobs from its PTT Telecom unit as part of a previously announced reorganisation of its telecom operations.
The jobs are to go from the Network Operations and Network Building arms of PTT Telecom with effect from October, a spokeswoman said.
PTT Telecom currently employs around 30,000 people, while the Dutch PTT group as a whole has around 90,000 employees.

The spokeswoman said Wednesday's announcement was a follow up to news last December that PTT Telecom was seeking to defend its margins in basic telecommunications services by cost cuts, adding the company wished to avoid compulsory redundancies.
The company said on Wednesday it planned to consolidate the 13 existing operational areas of PTT Telecom into five districts across the Netherlands.

To oversee the new networks control will be given to districts centred in Amsterdam, Rotterdam, Utrecht, Eindhoven and Zwolle. The building of new networks will be controlled by centres in Haarlem, Dordrecht, Gouda, Venlo and Groningen.
"As a consequence of the reorganisation some 400 jobs will be lost around the country from the Network Operations unit and around 700 from the Network Building unit," a statement said.
